flow.grossPlain: Mastercard reports revenue already net of the $5,631M of rebates and incentives it pays banks and merchants to win card business — so there is no separate cost-of-revenue line in its books. The costs were taken out before revenue was counted.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Salaries, technology and offices for the people who run the network — by far Mastercard's biggest cost. Tempered in part by new government grants recognized after agreements signed in late 2025.

opex.name: Advertising and marketing
opex.note: Brand campaigns, sponsorships and the 'Priceless' advertising.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, data centers, equipment and acquired technology.

opex.name: Provision for litigation
opex.note: Settlements with merchants who opted out of the U.S. merchant class litigation — Mastercard flags this as a special item.

follow100Note: The striking thing: Mastercard keeps $46.10 of every $100 — a net margin most businesses can only dream of — because the network's costs are mostly people and technology, not goods. But $5,631M of the $10,551M it billed in assessments went straight back to banks as rebates before revenue was even counted.
oneTimers: A $174M litigation provision — settlements with merchants who opted out of the U.S. merchant class litigation — is flagged by Mastercard as a special item. Excluding it and a $104M equity-investment loss, adjusted net income was $4.3B and adjusted EPS was $4.76.

G&A was tempered by new government grants recognized after agreements signed in late 2025, and other income includes a one-time tax-related interest benefit — both flagged in the release as favorable one-offs.
Mastercard bought back 6.4 million shares for $3.6B in the quarter and paid $684M in dividends.
otherDetail: Investment income of $86M and other income of $143M, outweighed by a $104M loss on equity investments and $159M of interest expense — net −$34M.

segments.name: Payment network
segments.note: The toll for running the card network — the fees banks pay per swipe, after the $5,631M of rebates Mastercard pays to win and keep card business. Gross assessments before those rebates were $10,551M: domestic $2,773M, cross-border $3,265M, transaction processing $4,241M.

segments.name: Value-added services and solutions
segments.note: Everything beyond the swipe: fraud screening, data analytics, consulting, identity and cybersecurity tools sold to banks and merchants — now 44% of net revenue and the fastest-growing part.

sources.label: Form 10-Q, 9 months ended Sep 30, 2025, revenue split (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Value-added services net revenue hit $3,886M — fraud tools, data and consulting now bring in 44 cents of every revenue dollar, and they grew more than twice as fast as the payment network itself (+12%).
takeaways.title: The services side is the growth engine

takeaways.text: Gross dollar volume grew 7% to $2.8 trillion, cross-border volume jumped 14% and switched transactions rose 10% — people are spending, and spending abroad.
takeaways.title: Cross-border is the volume story

takeaways.text: Mastercard repurchased 6.4 million shares for $3.6B in the quarter and paid $684M in dividends — returning $4.3B to shareholders in three months.
takeaways.title: The buyback machine kept running

verdict: Net revenue rose 18% to $8.8 billion as cross-border spending jumped 14% and value-added services grew 26% — and Mastercard kept $4.1 billion as profit, a 46% net margin.
